sonnet.problem: This card tells the brothers' offer in verse 9, 'he must die', and attaches jokes to it ('go ALL in' and 'never bet your life on a bag somebody else packed'). The joke is on the death line itself, which is a heavy moment.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: Verse 17 makes the same point as verse 10, which card 11 already asked: only the one found with the cup becomes a slave, and the rest go free. Card 20 asks that point a second time.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The question says 'the boy's brother', but no earlier card ever names or sets up 'the boy'. Benjamin also has many other brothers, so the question does not make clear which brother is meant.
sonnet.rule: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

sonnet.problem: The card gives Gen 42:29 as the source for what Jacob told his sons. That verse only says the brothers told Jacob what had happened. It does not say Jacob spoke the words about his two sons, so the reference does not support the fact it is attached to.
sonnet.rule: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.
